# Read From a File Using ifstream

#### Course: Learn C++ Intermediate

## Read From a File Using ifstream

In order to use the ifstream class, we first need to import the <fstream> header file. Then, we can create an ifstream object to open a file in read mode.

```cpp
// create ifstream object
ifstream my_file;

// open cpp.txt file in read mode
my_file.open("cpp.txt");
```

Notice that we don't need to supply ios::in as an argument to the open() function. This is because the open() function of ifstream has ios::in as a default argument.

![Idea Emoji](data:image/png;base64,)

Now, let's write a program to read from cpp.txt using ifstream.

```cpp
#include <iostream>

#include <fstream>

using namespace std;

int main() {

    string content;


    // create ifstream object
    ifstream my_file;

    // open file for reading
    my_file.open("cpp.txt");


    // check if the file has opened properly
    if (my_file.fail()) {

        // print error message
        cout << "File failed to load!";

        // exit the program
        exit(0);
    }


    // read until the End of File
    while (!my_file.eof()) {
        getline(my_file, content);
        cout << content << endl;
    }


    // close the file
    my_file.close();

    return 0;
}
```

Output

```text
C++ is awesome.
I love C++.
```
